note: Authored 2026-08-15 by the research-knowledge lane. Seventeen records fetched at source on that date, one per source the pack body, guides, refs, checks or exemplar make a claim on. The pack also cites fourteen rows that registry/evidence.json already holds (EV-0055, EV-0097, EV-0124, EV-0171, EV-0212, EV-0213, EV-0219, EV-0242, EV-0247, EV-0259, EV-0260, EV-0331, EV-0358, EV-0473); those are cited by their existing EV ids and are not re-recorded here, because a second row for a source already in the ledger is the drift this pack is against. The read surface cited FRAG- ids at authoring time because assigning EV ids is the integrator's step under ADR-0002 decision 3. That import has since run and no record deduplicated by URL against an existing row, so all seventeen arrived as new rows in fragment order, 01 to 17 becoming EV-0532 to EV-0548; the mapping table is in NOTES.md beside this file. The FRAG ids stay here because this is the pre-import record and check S014 exempts it, and rewriting one of the pair without the other would desync them. Three fetches were refused and none was worked around: the PMC copy of PRISMA 2020 served a bot check, and the BMJ copies of the PRISMA statement and of the 2024 Cochrane rapid-review recommendations each returned 403. The PLOS Medicine open-access copy of PRISMA was read instead and is FRAG-RESEARCH-KNOWLEDGE-01. No substitute was found for the rapid-review recommendations, so no record for them exists and the pack makes no claim resting on one.

records.source: Page and others, The PRISMA 2020 statement: an updated guideline for reporting systematic reviews (PLOS Medicine)
records.version_or_commit: PRISMA 2020, published 29 March 2021, superseding the 2009 edition
records.licence: CC BY 4.0, stated as the PLOS open-access licence on the article page
records.finding: A twenty-seven item checklist across seven sections, title, abstract, introduction, methods, results, discussion and other information, fixes what a synthesis has to disclose: why it was done, what was searched and when, what was included and excluded, and what was found. The authors state the scope narrowly. It governs reporting, it is not a guide to conducting a review, and it must not be used to judge a review's methodological quality. So a complete checklist is evidence that the work is inspectable and evidence of nothing else.
records.applicability_limits: Written for systematic reviews of health interventions, where the unit of evidence is a published study with a design and a population. A venture's sources are specifications, repositories and vendor documentation, so what transfers is the disclosure discipline rather than the method.
records.counter_evidence: The authors' own scope statement is the counter to over-reading the checklist: nothing in a fully completed PRISMA form says the review reached the right answer, and the statement says so in terms.

records.source: GRADE Working Group, the GRADE approach to rating certainty of evidence
records.version_or_commit: site as published on 2026-08-15, carrying a 2023-05 revision to the minimal requirements and a 2004 to 2026 copyright line
records.licence: not stated; the page carries a copyright line for the GRADE Working Group and publishes no reuse licence
records.finding: Certainty is rated in four bands, high, moderate, low and very low, and the rating attaches to the body of evidence answering one question rather than to any single source inside it. Five domains lower certainty: risk of bias, imprecision, inconsistency, indirectness and publication bias. Three can raise it: a large effect, a dose-response gradient, and residual bias that would push against the effect that was seen. The consequence for a knowledge base is that the grade belongs on the claim and not on the source, because the same source can support one claim strongly and another weakly.
records.applicability_limits: The domains are defined for healthcare intervention questions and at least one, dose response, has no analogue for a venture reading a specification. The four-band vocabulary transfers; most of the domain definitions do not.
records.counter_evidence: The Oxford levels record that hierarchies of evidence have been used inflexibly and criticised for decades, and that no ranking scheme works unless judgement is applied to its output. A four-band label applied without the domains behind it is exactly that failure.

records.source: OCEBM Levels of Evidence Working Group, Oxford Centre for Evidence-Based Medicine levels of evidence
records.version_or_commit: Levels of Evidence 2.1; the working group records the first version as produced in 1998 and revised since
records.licence: CC BY 4.0, stated on the University of Oxford page
records.finding: A five-level ranking of sources by study design, published with an introductory document the working group says must be read alongside the table rather than instead of it. The published caveat is the load-bearing part: a level may be moved down for quality, imprecision or indirectness and moved up for a large effect, and the group states plainly that no ranking scheme or decision aid works unless judgement is applied to its output.
records.applicability_limits: The levels name clinical study designs. The ladder a software venture actually climbs, the specification, then the implementation, then the maintainer's own statement, then somebody else's reading of it, is an analogy this pack draws and not something the source states.
records.counter_evidence: The working group publishes the criticism of hierarchies itself, so the source argues against its own naive use.

records.source: Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions, chapter 4, searching for and selecting studies
records.version_or_commit: Cochrane Handbook version 6.5.1, last updated March 2025, chapter 4
records.licence: not stated; the page carries a Cochrane Collaboration copyright line and publishes no reuse licence
records.finding: How much to search is answered by naming the cost of each limit rather than by naming a number. Searching one database is stated to be inadequate. Grey literature is put as highly desirable rather than required. Date cut-offs picked for convenience are advised against. Language limits are recorded as usually making little difference and as changing conclusions in three named fields, complementary medicine, psychiatry and rheumatology. Two people screening for inclusion is expected while two people running the search in parallel is said not to be desirable, which separates the recall problem from the judgement problem and spends the second reader only where judgement is being exercised.
records.applicability_limits: Written for a field with indexed literature and named databases. A venture searching vendor documentation and public repositories has no equivalent of a central register, so what transfers is the rule that every limit on the search is written down with what it might have cost.
records.counter_evidence: The chapter's own language finding cuts both ways. The usual case is that a language limit costs nothing and three fields are named exceptions, so a blanket refusal to limit is as unevidenced as a blanket limit.

records.source: Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions, chapter 22, prospective approaches to accumulating evidence
records.version_or_commit: Cochrane Handbook version 6.5, chapter 22, chapter last updated October 2019 in the 2024 handbook printing
records.licence: not stated; the page carries a Cochrane Collaboration copyright line and publishes no reuse licence
records.finding: A living review is one kept current by continual surveillance, with searches as often as monthly and newly found evidence folded in within roughly a month of being found. The handbook does not recommend the approach generally. It names three conditions that have to hold together: the question is high priority to the people deciding, certainty in what is currently held is low or very low, and new evidence is likely to arrive. Search method and expected update frequency are settled in the protocol rather than decided afresh each time.
records.applicability_limits: Health evidence, where the arrival rate of new studies drives the cadence. A venture's driver is a supplier shipping a new version or retiring an old one, which is event-driven rather than periodic, so a monthly cadence is the wrong shape even where the principle holds.
records.counter_evidence: The three conditions are themselves the counter to keeping everything living. A review kept current on a settled question spends continuous effort and never changes an answer.

records.source: Page, Higgins and Sterne, Cochrane Handbook chapter 13, assessing risk of bias due to missing results in a synthesis
records.version_or_commit: Cochrane Handbook version 6.5, chapter 13, last updated August 2024
records.licence: not stated; the page carries a Cochrane Collaboration copyright line and publishes no reuse licence
records.finding: Where whether a result got written up depends on what the result was, the surviving record systematically overstates benefit and understates harm. Two worked cases are given. Adding unpublished reboxetine trials more than doubled the estimated likelihood of withdrawal caused by adverse events. Unreported oseltamivir results changed the conclusions on hospital admission, on pneumonia and on psychiatric harms, so the direction of the answer reversed rather than merely softening. The recommended moves are comparing the protocol against the report, searching registers and regulatory documents rather than journals alone, treating funnel-plot asymmetry as one possible cause among several, and using a structured tool rather than an impression.
records.applicability_limits: Trials, with registries and regulators behind them. A venture has no equivalent register of the things somebody tried and did not write up, so what transfers is the direction of the bias and the habit of hunting the unreported result, not the instruments.
records.counter_evidence: The chapter states that funnel-plot asymmetry has causes other than non-reporting, so the commonest detection method is not diagnostic on its own and a clean funnel plot is not clearance.

records.licence: W3C Document Licence; the document carries a 2011 to 2013 W3C copyright line and states that W3C liability, trademark and document use rules apply
records.finding: Provenance is modelled as three kinds of thing and the relations between them: an entity, which is a thing whose aspects hold still; an activity, which happens over a stretch of time and acts on entities; and an agent, which is answerable for an activity happening. The starting-point relations are wasGeneratedBy, wasDerivedFrom, wasAttributedTo, used, wasInformedBy, wasAssociatedWith and actedOnBehalfOf. The stated purpose of recording any of it is to let a reader form an assessment of quality, reliability or trustworthiness, which is the argument for a record naming who did what to which source rather than naming only the source.
records.applicability_limits: An interchange ontology, not a workflow. It says nothing about which sources are good, how much evidence is enough, or what to do when a source stops resolving. Adopting the vocabulary without a process buys nothing.

records.source: GO FAIR, the FAIR guiding principles
records.version_or_commit: GO FAIR statement of the principles as published on 2026-08-15; the principles themselves date from the 2016 statement
records.licence: CC BY 4.0, stated by GO FAIR on the page
records.finding: Four groups of principles, of which two decide whether a knowledge base survives its sources. A2 states that metadata stay reachable even when the data they describe no longer are. R1.2 states that the description carries detailed provenance. F1 asks for a globally unique and persistent identifier and R1.1 for a clear and accessible usage licence. Read together they are the argument for the record outliving the source: when the page dies, the record is still a true fact about what was read, by whom, and when.
records.applicability_limits: Written for research data infrastructure with identifier services and repositories behind it. A venture usually has neither, so what transfers is the ordering rule that the record is the durable artefact rather than the machinery that would make it resolvable.
records.counter_evidence: The principles state properties and not thresholds. Nothing in them says how much metadata is enough, and a record can satisfy all four groups and still record something false.

records.version_or_commit: schema version 1.2.0; repository main branch as read on 2026-08-15, showing approximately 1,231 commits
records.finding: A plain-text file, readable by a person and by a machine, carrying the fields that make a software or dataset source re-findable later: title, authors with persistent author identifiers, version, date-released, repository URL, licence, and an identifiers block holding a DOI for one versioned snapshot rather than for the project in general. The hosting platform, archives and reference managers all read it, so the citation metadata travels attached to the artefact instead of living in somebody's notes.
records.applicability_limits: Software and datasets only. The format has no field for a finding, an applicability limit or counter-evidence, so it is a citation format and not an evidence record, and a venture that adopts it still needs somewhere to say what it concluded.

records.source: Klein and others, Scholarly Context Not Found: One in Five Articles Suffers from Reference Rot (PLOS ONE)
records.study_design: quantitative analysis of web references extracted from a scholarly corpus, tested for resolution and for archival coverage
records.population: over 3.5 million articles published between 1997 and 2012 drawn from arXiv, Elsevier and PubMed Central, yielding over one million extracted web references
records.licence: CC BY 4.0, stated as the PLOS open-access licence on the article page
records.finding: Two distinct failures are separated and named. Link rot is the reference no longer resolving at all. Content drift is the reference resolving to something that has since changed. Reference rot is either of them. Age dominates the rate: link rot ran at roughly three to five per cent for references in 2012 articles, depending on corpus, and at fifty-nine to eighty-nine per cent for references in 1997 articles. About one article in five suffers reference rot overall, and about seven in ten of those that carry any web reference at all.
records.applicability_limits: A scholarly corpus from 1997 to 2012. The rates measure academic web citation and not vendor documentation, which usually changes underneath a stable URL rather than disappearing, so the content-drift half is the relevant half for a venture and the link-rot rates are not transferable numbers.
records.counter_evidence: The authors state they had no real-world data on how often the referenced resources actually change, so the content-drift half rests on assumed temporal representativeness thresholds of one, thirty and three hundred and sixty-five days. The link-rot half is measured; the drift half is modelled, and the paper says so.
records.review: on-change-of:link rot and content drift literature

records.source: Van de Sompel, Nelson and Sanderson, RFC 7089, HTTP framework for time-based access to resource states, Memento
records.licence: IETF Trust Legal Provisions, BSD-style licence on code components; the document carries a 2013 IETF Trust and authors copyright line and is subject to BCP 78
records.finding: A way to ask the web for a resource as it was on a given date. The client sends an Accept-Datetime request header, a TimeGate negotiates on time and redirects, the archived state answers carrying a Memento-Datetime response header, and a TimeMap lists which states exist. The effect is to make the phrase the version I read into an address rather than a memory, which is what a record needs the day a claim resting on it is challenged.
records.applicability_limits: It works only where somebody archived the resource and runs a TimeGate for it. Nothing obliges a publisher to do either, so the framework describes how to ask and never guarantees an answer exists.

records.source: Vassilev, Oprea, Fordyce, Anderson, Davies and Hamin, NIST AI 100-2 E2025, Adversarial Machine Learning: A Taxonomy and Terminology of Attacks and Mitigations
records.version_or_commit: NIST AI 100-2 E2025, March 2025, DOI 10.6028/NIST.AI.100-2e2025; a planning note dated 3 June 2025 records an identified error on page x
records.licence: United States Government work; NIST publications are not subject to copyright in the United States
records.finding: The taxonomy separates direct prompt injection, where the hostile instruction arrives inside the request, from indirect prompt injection, where it is planted in something the system will later retrieve and read: a page, a document, a stored record, a message, a tool result. Mitigation is described as layered and as managing residual risk rather than removing it, and the document does not claim a complete defence exists.
records.applicability_limits: A taxonomy and a shared vocabulary. It does not rank mitigations by measured effectiveness, and it addresses AI systems in general rather than the research workflow specifically.
records.counter_evidence: The document's own erratum is the small lesson beside the large one. A maintained official source can be wrong on a numbered page and correct it three months later, so a record that pins the edition and the date can be re-checked and a citation that says NIST says cannot.

records.source: Greshake, Abdelnabi, Mishra, Endres, Holz and Fritz, Not what you've signed up for: compromising real-world LLM-integrated applications with indirect prompt injection
records.study_design: attack demonstrations against deployed and synthetic applications, with a threat taxonomy derived from them
records.population: a search-integrated chat assistant and code-completion engines, plus synthetic applications built for the study
records.model: GPT-4 and GPT-3 as integrated in the systems tested in 2023
records.version_or_commit: arXiv:2302.12173v2, submitted 23 February 2023, last revised 5 May 2023
records.finding: Once an application retrieves text and places it in front of a model, the boundary between the data being read and the instruction being followed stops being structural and becomes a matter of what the model decides. The demonstrated route needs no access to the interface at all: put the text where the system will fetch it. The taxonomy the paper draws from the demonstrations includes data theft, propagation between systems and contamination of the information the system will read next, which is the failure mode that matters for a knowledge base because it persists after the run that caused it.
records.applicability_limits: 2023 demonstrations against systems that have since changed, on models that have since been retired. The mechanism holds; the specific exploits evidence nothing about today's failure rates.
records.counter_evidence: The paper states that effective mitigations were lacking at the time of writing, which is no longer the position: later work in the ledger reports out-of-band defences cutting attack success substantially (EV-0214) and names structural patterns that constrain the action set before untrusted text is seen (EV-0473).

records.version_or_commit: page as last edited 14 August 2026 at 22:14 UTC
records.licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 for the text, with the page noting that additional terms may apply
records.finding: The three source classes are defined by distance from the thing rather than by quality. A primary source is close to the event and is often written by somebody involved in it. A secondary source sits at least one step removed and adds thought and reflection. A tertiary source summarises the other two. The operating rule that follows is the useful half: a primary source may carry a straightforward descriptive statement that an educated reader can check without specialist knowledge, and any interpretation of a primary source needs a secondary one, so an article resting mostly on primary sources is out of bounds.
records.applicability_limits: Written for an encyclopedia that forbids original research entirely, which is the opposite of a venture that has to reach its own conclusions and act on them. What transfers is the classification and the rule about interpretation, never the prohibition.
records.counter_evidence: For a software venture the ordering partly inverts. The specification and the source code are primary and are usually the most reliable things available, while the secondary reading is where the error enters. The policy's caution about primary sources is about interpretation and not about accuracy, and reading it the other way round is the mistake it invites.

records.version_or_commit: page as read on 2026-08-15, semi-protected and carrying policy status
records.licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 for the text, with the page noting that additional terms may apply
records.finding: The burden of showing a claim can be checked sits on whoever puts it in or puts it back, and it is discharged by one inline citation to a source that directly supports what was written. Material needing such a citation and carrying none may be taken out by anybody, and it should not be reinstated without one. Self-published and doubtful sources are admissible as information about themselves under stated conditions and are not evidence about anyone else.
records.applicability_limits: A volunteer project with an open edit model, high volume and an adversarial editing environment. A venture with three people has neither the volume nor the adversarial pressure the policy was written against, so the enforcement half is heavier than it needs.
records.counter_evidence: The removal rule works on a wiki because removal is cheap and reversible from history. In a knowledge base where removal loses the only copy of a finding, may be removed has to become is marked unsourced, or the policy destroys the evidence it exists to protect.

records.version_or_commit: proposal version 2, published 3 September 2024, page showing a modification date of 10 August 2026
records.licence: not stated; no licence line appears on the page or on the site's own llms.txt file
records.finding: A markdown file at a site's root listing what the site wants an AI reader to read, with links to clean markdown versions of its pages. The page tells whoever reads it that a machine reader should take the file first and then go to whichever of its links suit the question. That makes the file a source's own claim about which of its pages are authoritative and in what order, written in the imperative and addressed directly to the reader that will act on it. The file is fetched and parsed exactly like any other page, so nothing in the transport distinguishes the claim from a fact.
records.applicability_limits: A community proposal rather than a standard. There is no registry, no verification and no conformance test, and adoption is asserted rather than measured.
records.counter_evidence: A practitioner review of the same convention records that no major model provider has published documentation confirming the file is read at inference time, that the presence of the file showed no measurable effect on citation likelihood, and that instructions addressed to agents should be kept out of it.

records.version_or_commit: page marked last reviewed 27 May 2026 and maturity emerging, as read on 2026-08-15
records.finding: Practitioner guidance on the same convention that lands the opposite way on the question that matters here. Keep the file a curated index and keep system prompts, instructions addressed to agents and citation-preference directives out of it. The page records that no major provider has published documentation confirming the file is read at inference time, and that the presence of the file showed no measurable effect on how often a site was cited.
records.applicability_limits: One practitioner site. No method is published for the citation measurement it reports, and the page marks the whole convention as emerging, so the negative finding is a reason to doubt rather than a measurement to rely on.
records.counter_evidence: The proposal itself reports adoption by several major labs. Adoption is not the same claim as inference-time reading, but it is not nothing, and neither side of this is settled.
